This guide takes you from an assessment project folder to a tested ZIP for
PSYC40940. Read it alongside the formative assessment brief in the current NOW
learning room. Check that brief and the Dropbox for the deadline and any
year-specific instructions.

## What you are preparing

Prepare one RMarkdown report containing 3–4 visualisations using different
techniques. Explain what each shows, why you chose it, how its design relates
to effective visualisation principles, and what it may conceal. The current
formative limit is 1,000 words. The dashboard belongs to the summative assessment
only.

The report combines your own written explanation with R chunks that load the
data and generate the figures. Knitting it produces the HTML or PDF that the
reader sees. Keep both the editable source and its rendered output.

| Item to include | Example | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Exactly one RMarkdown report | `report.Rmd` | Contains your commentary and the code that generates your report |
| The rendered report | `report.html` or `report.pdf` | Lets the marker read the completed report and figures |
| RStudio project file | `formative-portfolio.Rproj` | Opens the project with its files together |
| Data used by the report | `data/behaviour.csv` | Allows the code to recreate the figures |
| Required supporting files | `references.bib`, `apa.csl`, or images used by the report | Supply these if your Rmd uses them |
| Completed GenAI declaration | `ai-declaration.pdf`, or the format specified on NOW | Records your use of GenAI; use the form supplied on NOW |

The filenames here are examples. Keep your own clear, neutral filenames and
make sure every path in your code matches them, including capital letters.
Follow the module's anonymity instructions when naming files and writing the
report.

## 1. Create or open your assessment project

Use a self-contained project for the assessment. The weekly module project is
useful for class work, but your submission should contain the files for your
own assessment rather than all the teaching materials.

To start a dedicated project in RStudio:

1. Choose File > New Project > New Directory > New Project.
2. Enter a neutral directory name such as `formative-portfolio`.
3. Choose a location you can find again and click Create Project.
4. Check the Files pane: it should contain `formative-portfolio.Rproj`.
5. Reopen this project in future by opening its `.Rproj` file.

If you already have a self-contained assessment project, use it. If your
assessment files are already together in a folder without a project file, use
File > New Project > Existing Directory and select that folder.

The `.Rproj` file records project settings; your report, code and data remain
separate files in the project folder. In Tools > Project Options > General,
disable restoring a saved workspace and choose not to save the workspace on
exit. Your report should recreate the objects it needs from its own code.

## 2. Put your data inside the project

1. In the project's Files pane, choose New Folder and create `data`.
2. Copy the actual data file into that folder using your computer's file manager.
3. Keep a record of the dataset's source and what one row represents.
4. Load that file from the Rmd using a relative path.

For a CSV called `behaviour.csv`, the import code in your report could be:

```{r csv-import-example, eval=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
my_data <- read_csv("data/behaviour.csv")
```

Use your actual filename. If the file is Excel, use an appropriate import
function such as `readxl::read_excel()` for `.xlsx`. Renaming a file's extension
does not convert its contents. Keep data preparation in the report so the marker
can see how the plotted data were obtained.

Use project-relative paths such as `data/behaviour.csv`. A path to your Downloads
folder or Desktop will not identify the data on another computer. Match `data`
and `Data` exactly; they can be different folders on another system.

If your dataset cannot be included because of access or redistribution
restrictions, agree an arrangement with the module leader before submission.
Include the source URL or DOI, exact filename, access/download steps and where
to place the file. Explain the arrangement in your report. Keep the import and
preparation code reproducible once the authorised file is available.

## 3. Create your RMarkdown report

1. Choose File > New File > R Markdown.
2. Choose an HTML document and give it a title about your data or question.
3. Leave the author field empty, following the anonymity instructions.
4. Save it as `report.Rmd` in the main project folder, beside the `.Rproj` file.
5. Replace the demonstration text and example chunks with your own report.

You may adapt a supplied formative template instead. Keep only your final
report Rmd in the submission, replacing its prompts, example dataset
descriptions and unrelated citations with your own work. Keep one YAML header
at the top of the file.

Write explanation and interpretation in the Markdown text. Use the Insert menu
above the Rmd editor to add R chunks for package loading, data import,
preparation and plots. Give chunks different names. Move the final code from
any exploratory R script into these chunks; running code in the Console alone
does not put it into the submitted report.

For each figure, tell the reader:

- the behavioural question it addresses;
- what its axes, groups and summaries represent;
- what pattern the visual evidence supports;
- why this view helps, compared with a plausible alternative;
- what information it hides or makes difficult to judge.

## 4. Knit and check the rendered report

1. Save `report.Rmd`.
2. Click Knit to generate `report.html` in the same folder.
3. Open the generated report and inspect every figure and its commentary.
4. Check labels, units, captions, figure references and the reference list.
5. Fix any error in the Rmd and knit again after your final edits.

The formative accepts HTML or PDF. If you submit PDF, include its Rmd source
and check the PDF itself. Your rendered file must correspond to your final
source, rather than an older successful render.

Load packages explicitly with `library()` in the report. Install any missing
packages before knitting, rather than making package installation part of each
render. Include any bibliography, citation-style or image files that your Rmd
uses. If rendering creates a required `report_files/` folder, keep it with the
HTML.

## 5. Complete the AI declaration from NOW

1. Open the Assessments section of the PSYC40940 NOW learning room.
2. Download the GenAI/AI usage declaration form provided there.
3. Complete it, explaining any permitted use of AI for code or troubleshooting.
   If you did not use GenAI, state that on the form.
4. Save the completed form in your assessment folder in the format requested
   on NOW. The example below calls it `ai-declaration.pdf`.
5. Include the completed form in your submission ZIP.

Use the supplied form and follow its specific completion instructions,
including any required identification fields. Your report commentary and
interpretation must be your own work, and GenAI is not a reference source.

## 6. Prepare the files to ZIP

Make a submission copy of your assessment folder in a separate location,
keeping your working project as a backup. Check the copy against this example:

```text
formative-portfolio/
  formative-portfolio.Rproj
  report.Rmd
  report.html
  ai-declaration.pdf
  data/
    behaviour.csv
  references.bib       (if used)
  apa.csl              (if used)
```

Include any other files your report genuinely needs, such as images or the
agreed data-access instructions. The example shows an HTML report; a PDF can
take its place. A file marked “if used” is needed only when your report uses it.

In the submission copy, remove unused exercise sheets, session guides, slides,
old report versions, unrelated data and exploratory scripts whose final code
has been incorporated into the Rmd. Exclude saved workspace/history files
such as `.RData` and `.Rhistory` and the temporary `.Rproj.user/` folder.
Keep exactly one final report Rmd and the `.Rproj` file.

## 7. Create the ZIP

Save your files, then close the assessment project. Use your computer's file
manager to locate the submission copy of the whole `formative-portfolio` folder.

| Computer | How to create the archive |
|---|---|
| Windows | Right-click the folder and choose its ZIP compression option. If needed, use Show more options > Send to > Compressed (zipped) folder. |
| Mac | Control-click or right-click the folder and choose Compress. |

This creates a file such as `formative-portfolio.zip`. Compressing the whole
folder keeps the data subfolder and file paths together. The ZIP should contain
your project folder and all its required files.

## 8. Test the extracted ZIP

Test the actual ZIP you intend to submit:

1. Extract it into a new location. On Windows, use Extract All; on Mac,
   double-click the ZIP and use the extracted folder.
2. Open the `.Rproj` inside that extracted copy. Work outside the ZIP itself.
3. Choose Session > Restart R so you begin without objects from earlier work.
4. Open the extracted `report.Rmd` and click Knit.
5. Open the newly generated report and check the figures and references.
6. Check that the extracted copy also contains the completed AI declaration.

If a file is missing or knitting fails, fix your working project and rebuild
the submission copy and ZIP. Test the new ZIP again. Repairing only the test
copy would leave the original ZIP unchanged.

## 9. Upload and keep the confirmation

Check these points before uploading:

- One final Rmd generates the report, including its plots and commentary.
- The rendered HTML or PDF matches that Rmd.
- The project, data or agreed access instructions, and required support files
  are present.
- The completed AI declaration from NOW is inside the ZIP.
- The report addresses the formative brief and stays within its word limit.
- The extracted copy has been tested, and filenames/content follow anonymity
  instructions.

Upload the tested ZIP to the formative Dropbox in NOW by the deadline in the
current brief. Complete the submission process, check the confirmation and keep
the receipt/email and a copy of the exact ZIP you submitted.
